title: Value a cash flow on the board's date

blocks.text: A regional water utility (invented for this practice) compares pipe projects at its board meeting. Each project's forecast is a dictionary `{calendar year: amount}` in $k, costs negative and savings positive, and some years have no entry at all. The board values every forecast on one date, the start of `on_year`, at a yearly rate `rate`. An amount booked in year `y` is paid at the start of `y`. Some forecasts start after the board's date; a few include money already paid in earlier years, which the board carries forward to its date at the same rate.
Write `value_on(flows, rate, on_year)`, returning the forecast's value on that date.

Write the formula first, in the notation of the lesson: the value of an amount $`\text{CF}_y`$ on the start of year $`y_0`$, and the sum over the forecast's years. Then check what it does for a year before $`y_0`$ and for a gap between years. About four lines.

from valuation import value_on

flows = {2030: -800, 2031: 250, 2033: 300, 2034: 350}

print("value on 2030 at 5%:", round(value_on(flows, 0.05, 2030), 3))
print("value on 2032 at 5%:", round(value_on(flows, 0.05, 2032), 3))
print("value on 2030 at 0%:", round(value_on(flows, 0.0, 2030), 3))
